programme.name: Computational Instrumentation and Scientific Control Systems
programme.question: How can human intent, mathematical representations, scientific computation, AI reasoning, and physical-system state be composed through minimal, verifiable representations?
programme.method: Build useful instruments and applications; record what each build tests; retain observations/counterexamples; promote only manually from hypothesis to pattern/principle/formal proposition; aggressively search for counterexamples.

records.title: Identity separation survives scientific transformations
records.statement: Scientific transformations that will be audited downstream require source identity, transformation identity, and output/result identity to remain separately addressable.
records.notes: Supported by current ClockSync and Calibration software experiments; not yet tested across the whole declared corpus.

records.title: ClockSync portable instrument qualification
records.statement: Test whether a source timestamp can survive a declared temporal-frame transformation while preserving source observation identity, model identity, uncertainty and result identity.
records.notes: Software qualification only; not physical metrological validation.

records.title: ClockSync retained source and derived coordinate separately
records.statement: The qualified ClockSync specimen retains the source observation/model while producing a separately identified reference-clock result with propagated uncertainty.
records.notes: Observation about software behavior.

records.title: Calibration portable instrument qualification
records.statement: Test whether raw, indicated and calibrated measurement representations remain distinguishable while the declared affine transform propagates full joint first-order uncertainty.
records.notes: Software qualification only; not a physical calibration certificate.

records.title: Calibration retained raw, indicated and corrected values
records.statement: The qualified Calibration specimen preserves raw, indicated and corrected measurement values as distinct fields while retaining the affine operation and uncertainty budget.
records.notes: Observation about software behavior.

records.title: Transformations should preserve the identities required to audit meaning
records.statement: When downstream reasoning depends on provenance or transformation semantics, the representation should preserve separately addressable source, transformation and result identities rather than collapse them into one value.
records.notes: Provisional generalization from H-001; deliberately narrower than claiming every software transformation always needs the same metadata.

records.title: Human interpretation can seed computation without becoming evidence
records.statement: Human annotations can be made computationally addressable and used to seed an investigation while remaining epistemically distinct from evidence, canonical state, verification and execution authority.
records.notes: Current evidence is the typed annotation plus annotation→NISE→NET loop.

records.title: Annotation to NISE to NET composition
records.statement: Test whether a human annotation can become typed investigation intent, construct a NISE schematic, and compile to a NET experiment contract while truth/execution authority remain false.
records.notes: No provider executed during this qualification.

records.title: Annotation remained non-evidence across the full planning loop
records.statement: The qualified loop carried annotation identity, evidence/model refs and requested semantic operations through NISE/NET planning while retaining physical_truth_established=false and execution_authority=false.
records.notes: Supports H-002.

records.title: Query-conditioned graph reduction can retain explicit unresolved structure
records.statement: A bounded query-conditioned structural reduction can expose a smaller relevant graph while retaining unresolved capabilities and blocked frontier structure instead of fabricating completeness.
records.notes: Current evidence is NISE V1 synthetic qualification; domain-general sufficiency remains untested.

records.title: NISE bounded schematic compiler V1
records.statement: Test deterministic explicit focus/capability graph expansion with hop/node budgets and hypothesis policy.
records.notes: Question text is retained but does not secretly select nodes in V1.

records.title: NISE retained unresolved capability and blocked hypothesis frontier
records.statement: The qualified NISE fixture retained unavailable requested operations and hypothesis-policy frontier entries rather than silently inventing or discarding them.
records.notes: Supports H-003 but does not demonstrate same-answer fidelity on a real domain.

records.title: Every transformation requires covariance
records.statement: Every representation transformation requires a covariance object.
records.notes: Intentionally retained as an over-generalization that fails outside numerical uncertainty-bearing transformations.

records.title: Human annotation transformations do not inherently require covariance
records.statement: Creating/superseding a typed human annotation transforms interpretive state and identity while its semantics do not inherently include numerical covariance.
records.notes: Counterexample motivates a narrower uncertainty-preservation principle.

records.title: Uncertainty semantics must be preserved when uncertainty is part of the source meaning
records.statement: When uncertainty is part of the source semantics and relevant to downstream computation, a transformation should explicitly propagate, preserve, bound, or refuse that uncertainty rather than silently discard it.
records.notes: Refinement prompted by the failure of H-004; not claimed universal.

records.title: A backend-neutral container contract can preserve computational boundary semantics
records.statement: A common container specification can preserve typed boundaries, semantic operations, authority constraints, resource envelopes and telemetry requirements independently of whether an occurrence runs locally, in an OS/container runtime, on HPC, in cloud infrastructure, or through an external provider.
records.notes: V1 has contract-level qualification only. Real cross-backend occurrences remain required before stronger generalization.

records.title: Container / Experiment Calculus V1 qualification
records.statement: Test typed container boundaries, acyclic nesting, exact schema/unit/frame flows, resource telemetry, explicit uncertainty proxies, and backend-neutral occurrence identity without binding execution or inferring physical theory.
records.notes: 25 tests passed on Ubuntu and Windows; this is an engineering-contract experiment, not FEP evidence.

records.title: Container telemetry kept transport accounting separate from workload-defined uncertainty
records.statement: The qualified Container Calculus kept byte/item transport ratios distinct from explicitly declared posterior-entropy reduction, retained unknown GPU/energy/human metrics as unknown, and did not infer a universal information score.
records.notes: Supports a clean engineering boundary between resource transport and workload-specific information measures.

records.title: Adaptive multi-scale precision can dominate maximal precision for bounded decisions
records.statement: For a fixed decision task and declared acceptance/validity constraints, there exist workloads where a lower-cost representation or scale preserves the required outputs, invariants, epistemic distinctions and verification while consuming fewer scarce resources than a uniformly higher-fidelity representation.
records.notes: Open hypothesis. It should be tested with same-task full-vs-reduced representation experiments; no claim is made that lower fidelity is always sufficient.

records.title: Same-task oscillator full-vs-NISE-reduced execution
records.statement: Execute the same retained oscillator analysis task through a broad eight-operation baseline and a NISE-selected two-operation graph; require identical required statistics/periodogram outputs, contracts, source evidence identity and provider runtime before comparing resource use.
records.notes: Controlled redundancy experiment on the real built-in oscillator provider; wall-time observations are retained but not generalized.

records.title: Query-conditioned reduction preserved required oscillator results while executing fewer operations
records.statement: Across Ubuntu and Windows, NISE reduced the source catalog from 9 nodes to a 3-node schematic and NET execution from 8 operations to 2 while preserving the required statistics/periodogram data, operation contracts, source-evidence identity within each trial pair and provider runtime identity.
records.notes: Operation-call ratio was 0.25. Hosted wall-time ratios were ~0.258 and ~0.244 but are not treated as stable performance claims.

relations.notes: ClockSync tests identity separation under time-frame transformation.
Calibration tests identity separation under measurement transformation.
Repeated identity separation motivates a candidate principle.
Full planning loop tests human interpretation boundary.
NISE V1 tests bounded structural reduction.
Broad covariance universal fails on annotation transformation.
Rejected over-generalization motivates narrower uncertainty semantics.
Container Calculus V1 tests the backend-neutral contract at schema/telemetry level.
Telemetry qualification supports separation of boundary semantics from one runtime/backend.
Adds a physical-system same-task fidelity test to the NISE reduction hypothesis.
Required outputs/contracts/evidence/runtime were preserved under query-conditioned reduction in the oscillator workload.
